title: Hockey Stick Galaxy NGC 4656
caption: The Hockey Stick Galaxy, NGC 4656, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter telescope at Kitt Peak
celestial: Hockey Stick Galaxy, NGC 4656 · constellation Canes Venatici

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: NGC 4656 is a spiral galaxy seen edge-on, but its disc is bent out of shape, giving it the look that earned it the informal nickname of the hockey stick galaxy. A faint object sits in the upper-left corner of the image.

The galaxy's unusual shape comes from a recent gravitational encounter with another galaxy, NGC 4631. The two may have begun to merge, though that is not yet certain. The faint object at the upper left may not belong to NGC 4656 at all. Instead it may be a dwarf galaxy that is itself in the process of merging with it.

When galaxies pass close to each other, their gravity pulls on stars and gas, stretching and warping their discs. Seen edge-on, like this one, such distortions are especially easy to spot, because a normal disc would appear as a straight, thin line. NGC 4656 lies in the constellation Canes Venatici.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter telescope observed NGC 4656 through B, V, I and hydrogen-alpha filters, shown as blue, green, orange and red respectively.
